solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Infection restricting any number, bringing growls once

indicators.note: to restrict something is to hem it in, so one word closes round the other

parts.note: SARS is the respiratory infection
n stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: An infection limiting numbers makes patients grumble and growl.
explanation.walkthrough: SARS goes round N. 'Once' marks the word as obsolete: to snar was to snarl.
explanation.definitionFit: Snar is an archaic verb meaning to snarl, so snars is the old third-person form for growls.

clue.text: Thus a place like Cairo shows dryness

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus
Cairo is a city

explanation.surface: A desert city like Cairo is notably dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Siccity, from Latin siccus 'dry', is a rare word for aridity.

clue.text: Lily ran up excitedly to hug Henry

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping round, so one part encloses the other
doing something excitedly is agitated, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Lily dashed over in excitement to embrace Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lily' looks like a woman's name but is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuphar is the genus of yellow water lilies, so it names a kind of lily.

clue.text: Mechanic's having to repair train, alas

indicators.note: repairing something means taking it apart and putting it back together

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mechanic sadly has to fix a broken train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mechanic's' is the possessive, 'belonging to a mechanic', not 'mechanic has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanic in the old sense is a manual worker or craftsman, and artisanal means relating to such a craftsman.

clue.text: Fattened and fully satisfied, having swallowed a drink

indicators.note: a thing swallowed ends up inside, so the drink goes within

parts.note: sated means fully satisfied
a + gin, a drink

explanation.surface: Someone well fed and content after downing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Saginate is a rare verb, from Latin saginare, meaning to fatten livestock.

clue.text: Disturbed seabird snaps?

indicators.note: something disturbed has been knocked out of its settled order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A seabird, upset, starts snapping at people.
explanation.walkthrough: Darbies is old slang for handcuffs; the question mark admits that 'snaps' for handcuffs, which snap shut on the wrists, is a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Handcuffs click shut on the wrists, so they can be whimsically called snaps; darbies is the slang term for handcuffs.

clue.text: Title of honour given for penning superior bit of poetry

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as sheep in a pen, so one part holds the other

parts.note: Dan is an old title like Master, as in Dan Chaucer
U means upper-class, superior

explanation.surface: An honour awarded for writing a fine piece of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A duan is a Gaelic poem or a canto, a division of a long poem.

clue.text: Like piece of furniture that's rickety?

parts.note: as means like
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Describing a wobbly piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'rickety' stands loosely for unstable.
explanation.definitionFit: Astable means not stable, unable to stay in one state, so something rickety can be called astable.

clue.text: Sailor standing up with quiver, old boy coming out for decoration

indicators.note: in a down light standing up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: coming out means leaving, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: to quiver is to wobble
OB stands for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A sailor stands trembling as an old boy receives a decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: AB turned up becomes BA, then WOBBLE loses OB.
explanation.definitionFit: Bawble is an old spelling of bauble, a showy trinket or ornament.

clue.text: Old lord and freeman getting caught out

indicators.note: out means removed, so the cricket letter for caught is struck off

parts.note: a ceorl was a freeman of the lowest rank in Anglo-Saxon England
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A lord and a freeman both caught in the act.
explanation.definitionFit: Eorl is the Old English word for a nobleman, the forerunner of earl.

clue.text: Handle of alloy twisted at the end

indicators.note: only the tail is twisted, so just the last letters change places

parts.note: steel is an alloy of iron

explanation.surface: A metal handle, bent at the tip.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the last two letters of STEEL swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: Stele (also steal or steil) is a dialect word for the handle or shaft of a tool.

clue.text: Unchaste politician being cut off by law

indicators.note: something cut off is removed, so the politician is taken out of the word for unchaste

parts.note: unchaste means impure
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An immoral politician is legally removed from office.
explanation.walkthrough: IMPURE loses MP to leave IURE. The blog copy reads 'out off', a slip for 'cut off'.
explanation.definitionFit: Iure (jure) is the Latin ablative of ius, so it translates as 'by right' or 'by law', as in de iure.

clue.text: Something round hidden by stone is onion

indicators.note: a thing hidden by another is covered by it, so one set of letters sits inside the other

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight (14 lb)
a halo is a ring of light

explanation.surface: A round object buried under a stone turns out to be an onion.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds, abbreviated in the usual way.
explanation.definitionFit: Shalot is an old spelling of shallot, a small mild variety of onion.

clue.text: Knowing about Scottish street supplying ceramic

indicators.note: about means going around, so the knowing word surrounds the street

parts.note: knowing means aware
gate is a Scots and northern word for a street

explanation.surface: A street in Scotland known for supplying pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: Gate for street survives in Scottish and northern English place names, such as Gallowgate in Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: Agateware is pottery streaked to resemble agate, so it is a kind of ceramic.

clue.text: Hard material child's given at home

parts.note: a chit is a young child, especially a cheeky girl; the 's is read as 'is'
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A child is handed something hard while staying at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'child's' is read as 'child is', so CHIT is followed by IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Chitin is the tough substance that forms the shells of insects and crustaceans.

clue.text: Criminal is pinned by gun, as shown by artist

indicators.note: something pinned by another is held fast within it

parts.note: a Colt is a make of revolver
an old lag is a habitual criminal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A criminal held at gunpoint, as depicted by an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like an adjective for the gun but is a noun in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: A collagist makes collages, pictures built from pasted scraps, so is a kind of artist.

clue.text: One crushed by warhorse on the move — it comes down in a flash

definitions.text: it comes down in a flash

indicators.note: something crushed by another is squeezed inside it
moving letters rearrange them

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone trampled by a charging warhorse, struck down in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like rain or lightning, but describes a burst of particles.
explanation.definitionFit: An air shower is the cascade of particles a cosmic ray triggers in the atmosphere, raining down almost instantly.

clue.text: Biochemical substance breaking down in a tail bone

indicators.note: breaking down suggests falling to pieces and being reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemical decomposing within the coccyx.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking down' suggests catabolism, the opposite of the answer's own process, which is a nice irony.
explanation.definitionFit: An anabolite is a substance formed in anabolism, the building-up stage of metabolism.

clue.text: Track blocked by a very small sledge

indicators.note: a path blocked by something has that thing lodged within it

parts.note: a trail is a track
taken as written
v is the short form of very; 'small' signals the abbreviation

explanation.surface: A trail is obstructed by a tiny sledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travail' usually means toil; the sledge sense is a rare variant that the definition relies on.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is a variant of travois, a sledge-like frame dragged by a horse or dog among Plains peoples.

clue.text: Sheathe naughty child well into the night?

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
late describes a time well into the night

explanation.surface: Tuck in a naughty child who is still up very late.
explanation.definitionFit: To implate is to cover with plates, as in armour, so it means sheathe.

clue.text: Memory again coming back

indicators.note: something coming back retraces its route, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: more can mean again, as in 'once more'

explanation.surface: A recollection returns once more.
explanation.definitionFit: EROM stands for erasable read-only memory, a type of computer memory chip.

clue.text: Oxford college sounds so mawkish

indicators.note: sounds tells us to go by how the college's name is spoken

parts.note: Magdalen College, Oxford, is pronounced the same as the answer

explanation.surface: An Oxford college seems overly sentimental.
explanation.walkthrough: Magdalen College's name is famously not pronounced as spelt; the adjective comes from weeping Mary Magdalene.
explanation.definitionFit: Maudlin means tearfully sentimental, which is what mawkish means too.

clue.text: Tree in Himalayan garden

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A tree growing in a Himalayan garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The yang is a large Asian timber tree, a dipterocarp yielding gurjun oil.

clue.text: With work inside, most of the paint drips

indicators.note: inside places the work within the paint word
most of means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: gloss is a shiny paint
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Working with paint, most of it runs.
explanation.walkthrough: GLOSS shortened to GLOS holds OP.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloops is an informal plural or verb for gooey globs or the act of dripping thickly.

clue.text: Male priest, someone daft about female

parts.note: m is the abbreviation for male
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the daft person is read backwards

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A male priest and a fool fussing over a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single last word: a girl's name stands for any female.
explanation.definitionFit: Melissa is a woman's given name, so it stands for a female in the style these puzzles use.

clue.text: Saw sports grounds — fund finally provided for one

indicators.note: provided for means supplied in place of, so one letter swaps for another

parts.note: stadia is a plural of stadium

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word it follows

parts.note: finally keeps only the last letter
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone saw the sports grounds, with a fund finally put up for one of them.
explanation.walkthrough: In STADIA the I gives way to D. 'Saw' looks like a past tense; it is the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadda is a double-bladed hand saw used by comb-makers.

clue.text: Sozzled chap drinking beer, one of a type of creature immersed in the drink?

definitions.text: of a type of creature immersed in the drink?

indicators.note: drinking means taking something inside, so the beer goes within
a sozzled person is drunk and jumbled, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
ale is a beer
an means one, as in 'an apple'

explanation.surface: A drunk man downing beer like a creature at home in drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is slang for the sea, where jellyfish live.
explanation.definitionFit: Acalephan is the adjective for the acalephs, an old name for jellyfish, which float in the sea.

clue.text: Pest beginning to plague hospital — get external help

indicators.note: external help is help wrapped around the outside

parts.note: aid is help

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: only the first letter is kept
h is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A plague begins in a hospital and outside help is called in.
explanation.walkthrough: P and H sit inside AID.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids are sap-sucking insects that damage garden plants, so they are a classic pest.

clue.text: Flier some miles up

parts.note: m is the abbreviation for miles

indicators.note: in a down light up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: some can mean any, as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: A plane or bird some miles up in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The myna is a starling-like Asian bird, so it is a flier.

clue.text: Group of eight perform in old tribe

parts.note: o is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: Gad was one of the twelve tribes of Israel
to do is to perform

explanation.surface: Eight people performing in an ancient tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: Gad was one of the twelve tribes of Israel, a regular crossword tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogdoad comes from the Greek for eight and means a set of eight things or beings.

clue.text: Note as before the difference between Mary and May

indicators.note: before sets the first piece ahead of the second in the answer

parts.note: the Roman as was the basic unit, one whole

parts.words: the difference between Mary and May
parts.note: Mary is May with this one letter added

explanation.surface: A musical note as it was written before, with the gap between two girls' names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note as before' reads like an instruction to repeat; 'as' is taken as the Roman unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Oner is slang for a one-pound note, a single unit of currency.

clue.text: I am a phony, suffering from a mild form of madness

indicators.note: suffering suggests being in a disturbed, unsettled state

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being a fake and to a little madness.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypomania is a milder state of mania, with elevated mood but without full psychotic features.

clue.text: Writer may want this in back of book, page with holy text

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: only the final letter of book is kept
p is the abbreviation for page
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: An author wants something in the back of the book, a page of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer looks like an author but is someone writing with pen and ink.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone writing with a dip pen needs a pot of ink to dip into.

clue.text: African money disposed of, beginning to end

indicators.note: the first letter is sent to the back of the word

parts.note: iced is slang for killed, disposed of

explanation.surface: Some African cash got rid of from start to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: The cedi is the currency unit of Ghana in West Africa.

clue.text: Expert not well, suffering relapse — back shortly

indicators.note: a relapse is a falling back, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: bad means unwell, as in feeling bad

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: An expert feeling poorly has had a relapse and will be back soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like part of 'back shortly' meaning returning soon, but it is the rear of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A dabster is a dialect word for an expert, related to 'dab hand', a skilled person.

clue.text: An old-fashioned despot and a knight following god of war

indicators.note: following places the later pieces after the god's name

parts.note: Tyr is the Norse god of war
taken as written
N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A tyrant of old and a knight serving under the god of war.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyran is an obsolete spelling of tyrant, a cruel absolute ruler.
